You must end this movement in {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Trick Shooter
entries: You learn a number of trick shots you can use to debilitate enemies and impress allies. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a trick shot.

Some of your trick shots require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the trick shot's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Trick Shot save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier

entries.name: Blinding Shot
entries: You attempt to blind the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Brutal Shot
entries: You attempt to knock the target prone. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Hampering Shot
entries: You attempt to hobble the enemy's movement. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Spinning Flourish
entries: You can {@optfeature Flourish|sw5e-phb|flourish} your weapon in an intimidating or charming manner. As an action, you can cause one creature within 60 feet to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Ricochet Shot
entries: You learn how to work all the angles. Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action and miss with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can repeat the attack against a different target within 10 feet of the original target (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Quickdraw
entries: You learn to perform miracles with just a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} and some nerve. On your first turn in combat, if you aren't surprised, you can use your action to attack creatures that have not yet acted. Choose up to six such creatures that you can see, making a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against each. On a hit, you deal normal weapon damage and can apply a single trick shot to each attack made this way.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Heavy Weapons Specialist
entries: Some manned instruments of war require their user to have superior physical prowess to overcome their weight and encumbrance. Those fighters who choose to become Heavy Weapons Specialists use their powerful bodies, and powerful armaments, to overwhelm their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Rock Steady
entries: You have learned to use the heft of your weapon to root yourself in place. At the end of each of your turns, if you move less than half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained}, moved, or knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. This {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} lasts until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: My Little Friend Says Hello There
entries: You know how to use the sheer size of your weapon to strike fear in those around you. You can add your Strength modifier to any Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) check you make while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties.

subclassFeature.name: Maximum Output
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties, you can forgo one or more attacks. If you do so, the first time you deal damage with the weapon before the start of your next turn, you deal additional damage of the same type as the weapon's damage. If this instance would deal damage to multiple creatures, you can only apply this additional damage to one of them. For each attack you forgo, you deal additional damage equal to 1d12 + half your fighter level. If you miss with the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make before the end of your next turn, or one target succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your weapon's burst or rapid property, you instead deal normal weapon damage.

subclassFeature.name: Straight Through
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} on your turn while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties, you can make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against a creature within 5 feet of the target using your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Overwhelm
entries: When you use your Second Wind while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties, if you hit with the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make, or if one creatures fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your weapon's burst or rapid property, before the end of your next turn, you treat the hit as a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}. If you miss with the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make before the end of your next turn, or one target succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your weapon's burst or rapid property, you instead deal normal weapon damage.

subclassFeature.name: Pure Performance
entries: At 18th level, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} you make while wielding a weapon with the heavy or strength properties can't suffer from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

subclassFeature.name: Illusionist Technique
entries: Among the galaxy you may find the various infiltrators and agents who make ample use of holographic technology to get themselves in and out of danger. Followers of the Illusionist Technique make use of this holographic technology to give themselves an illusory edge in combat.

subclassFeature.name: Holographic Decoy
entries: As an action, you can create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 10 minutes, or until you lose your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} (as if you were concentrating on a power). The decoy appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. The decoy is purely visual. If anything passes through it, it is revealed to be an illusion. For the duration, you can cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} as though you were in the decoy's space. Both your decoy and the target of your {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} must be within your line of sight.

You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to cause the decoy to move up to 30 feet. As your decoy changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the decoy. If your decoy is ever more than 120 feet away from you, it immediately disappears.

Additionally, when both you and your decoy are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the decoy, but is not aware it is an illusion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature.

A creature that uses its action to examine your decoy can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Holographic Decoy
entries: As an action, you can create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 10 minutes, or until you lose your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} (as if you were concentrating on a power). The decoy appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. The decoy is purely visual. If anything passes through it, it is revealed to be an illusion. For the duration, you can cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} as though you were in the decoy's space. Both your decoy and the target of your {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} must be within your line of sight.

You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to cause the decoy to move up to 30 feet. As your decoy changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the decoy. If your decoy is ever more than 120 feet away from you, it immediately disappears.

Additionally, when both you and your decoy are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the decoy, but is not aware it is an illusion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature.

A creature that uses its action to examine your decoy can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check against your tech save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Illusionist
entries: The target of your Ranger's Quarry feature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on all checks made to discern the nature of your illusions. Additionally, when the target of your Ranger's Quarry is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to immediately cause an active illusion, or your Holographic Decoy, to take the form of the creature as long as the creature's dimensions fall within the power's capacity restrictions.

subclassFeature.name: Charged Illusions
entries: When a creature discerns the nature of an illusion you have created using a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or class feature while within 5 feet of it, you can dispel the illusion (no action required) to have the creature take energy damage equal to 1d10 + half your scout level.

subclassFeature.name: Quick Escape
entries: Whenever you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to swap places with an illusion of yourself that you have created using a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or class feature. The illusion must be within 60 feet of you, and you must be able to see it.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Decoys
entries: You can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use your Holographic Decoy feature. When you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to move a decoy, you can move any number of them with the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Industrial Approach
entries: While some berserkers are content to surrender to their rage, others prefer a more tactful approach. Berserkers of the Industrial Approach augment their rage with the versatility of technology, adding elemental explosions to their already fearsome arsenal.

subclassFeature.name: Techcasting
entries: You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your berserker level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Industrial Approach {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Player's Handbook) as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

subclassFeature.name: Industrious Tech
entries: You can cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while raging as long as the power's casting time is no more than 1 action and the power does not require {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. While raging, you add your rage damage to damage rolls from {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that require a tech attack or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} damages more than one target, you may only apply your rage damage to one of them.

Casting {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} during rage counts as attacking for the purposes of maintaining rage, and you can use your Reckless Attack feature to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} when casting a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires a tech attack.

subclassFeature.name: Explosive Resilience
entries: Once per round, when you deal damage that includes your rage damage, you can cause a localized {@spell Explosion|sw5e-phb|explosion} around the recipient of that damage. Each creature within 5 feet of the damaged creature other than you takes acid, cold, fire, ion, or lightning damage (your choice) equal to your rage damage bonus, and you gain {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to the chosen damage type until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Painkiller
entries: Whenever you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-level or higher, or deal damage using your Explosive Resilience feature, you can cause a friendly creature you can see within 30 feet to gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to half your berserker level + your Intelligence modifier. Additionally, while they have these temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, they have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would cause them to be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}.

subclassFeature.name: Final Countdown
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} but not killed outright, and you have at least one tech point remaining, you can expend all your remaining tech points and instead to drop to one hit point (no action required). If you do so, each creature within 30 feet of you must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, they take 1d12 acid, cold, fire, ion, or lightning damage (your choice) damage for each tech point spent in this way, or half as much on a successful one.

subclassFeature.name: Inquisitor Technique
entries: Across history, there have been those who live to hunt those who wield the Force, be they Jedi or Sith. Followers of the Inquisitor Technique combine technology with force techniques to track down and eliminate force-wielders. For those practitioners of the Force, they are the greatest adversary.

subclassFeature.name: Forcecasting Secrets
entries: You have learned secrets from a subtle attunement to the force. Choose two {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of no higher level than your Max Power Level, as shown in the scout table. The chosen powers count as {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for you, but are not included in the number in the Powers Known column of the scout table.

You learn two additional powers at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you know and replace it with another {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of no higher level than your Max Power Level.

entries: When the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature is within 15 feet of you, you gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever the creature casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, it must first succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. On a failed save, the casting is disrupted, the {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} fails, and the force points are wasted.

On a failed save, it loses {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on the power.

entries: The radius of this feature increases to 30 feet at 11th level and 60 feet at 17th level.

entries: You can cast the {@i force suppression} and {@i sever force} {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 3rd level against the target of your Ranger's Quarry without expending tech points. If they are within 30 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check for these powers.

subclassFeature.name: Jal Shey Order
entries: Monks of the Jal Shey order, driven by the pursuit of knowledge, maintain one of the most well-respected and heavily guarded repositories of history and knowledge across the galaxy: the Archives of the Jal Shey. Here, young folk of all species seeking the clarity of truth and the strength of knowledge pledge to learn the arts of seeking enlightenment by understanding the world around them, and mastering the techniques to defend it. To become a Jal Shey monk is to give one's self to the quest for unveiling the deepest mysteries of the galaxy, to bring light to the secrets of the dark, and guard the most powerful and dangerous of truths.

subclassFeature.name: Mystical Erudition
entries: You've undergone extensive training in lore from the Jal Shey's collected knowledge. You learn one language of your choice, and you gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}. You learn an additional language and an additional skill proficiency from the above list at 11th level.

Additionally, you can strike multiple pressure points to extract crucial details about your foe. Whenever you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can learn learn certain information about its capabilities. The GM tells you if the creature has one of the following characteristics of your choice:

items: Condition immunities
Damage vulnerabilities
Damage resistances
Damage immunities

subclassFeature.name: Extort Truth
entries: You can hit a series of hidden nerves on a creature with precision, temporarily causing them to be unable to mask their true thoughts and intent. When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can have the attack deal no damage and spend 1 focus point to force them to make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your focus save DC. On a failed save, the creature is unable to speak a deliberate lie for 1 minute and all Charisma checks directed at the creature are made with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} for the duration.
On a success or failure, a creature is aware that you attempted to influence them. They can choose to avoid answering questions to which they would normally respond with a lie.

subclassFeature.name: Preternatural Counter
entries: Your quick mind and study of your foe allows you to use their failure to your {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. When a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with a melee attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make an unarmed strike against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Mercurial Mind
entries: You've honed your awareness and reflexes through mental aptitude and pattern recognition. Once per turn, if you've already used your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, you can spend 1 focus point to take an additional {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}. You can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Debilitating Barrage
entries: You've gained the knowledge to temporarily inhibit a creature's fortitude by striking a series of pressure points. Whenever you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 focus points to cause the creature to become vulnerable to a damage type of your choice. This effect lasts for 1 minute or until they take damage of the chosen type.

subclassFeature.name: Jar'Kai Form
entries: {@optfeature Jar'Kai Form|sw5e-phb}, also known as Domination Form, utilizes two weapons to overwhelm their foes. Those guardians who focus on {@optfeature Jar'Kai Form|sw5e-phb} know that two weapons offer greater versatility than one, and capitalize on the twin angles from which they attack to subdue their enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Form Basics
entries: You gain the Jar'Kai {@book lightsaber form, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of the Player's Handbook. If you already know this form, you can instead choose another {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}.

subclassFeature.name: The Way of the Acklay
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can enter a destructive stance for one minute. While in this stance, you can add half your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to any melee weapon damage roll you make that doesn't already include that modifier. Additionally, when you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can move up to 5 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You gain the following Channel the Force option.

entries.name: Twin Strike
entries: Once per turn, when you miss with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force to immediately make another {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against the same target (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Eye of the Storm
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you regain an expended use of your Channel the Force.

subclassFeature.name: Rising Whirlwind
entries: As an action, you can rush forward up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. Each creature within 5 feet of your path must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with your weapon). A creature takes normal weapon damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. If you are wielding separate two light- or vibro-weapons in each hand with which you are proficient, or a weapon with the double property, a creature makes this save with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, and takes additional damage equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice, minimum of one) on a failed save if it doesn't already include that modifier.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Domination
entries: You are a {@spell Whirlwind|sw5e-phb|whirlwind} of strikes, eviscerating all who step within your reach. Your Strength and Dexterity scores increase by 2. Your maximum for these scores increases by 2. Additionally, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic, energy, and ion damage from weapons.

When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} roll you make against that creature, and that creature provokes an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} from you even if they take the {@action Disengage|sw5e-phb} action before leaving your reach until the end of your next turn.
Creatures provoke an {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} from you when they enter your reach.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Juyo/Vaapad Form
entries: Juyo/{@optfeature Vaapad Form|sw5e-phb}, also known as Ferocity Form, revels in the satisfaction of battle and victory. Those guardians who focus on Juyo/{@optfeature Vaapad Form|sw5e-phb} channel their emotions into their fighting, making heavy, sweeping strikes.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

subclassFeature.name: Form Basics
entries: You gain your choice of the Juyo or Vaapad {@book lightsaber form, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of the Player's Handbook. If you already know the chosen form, you can instead choose another {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}.

subclassFeature.name: The Way of the Vornskr
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can take a savage stance, designating one creature you can see within 10 feet of you as your prey for 1 minute. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against the creature. If the target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on a subsequent turn to mark a new creature.

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You gain one of the following Channel the Force options. Choose Snap Aggression for Juyo or Assertive Defense for Vaapad.

entries.name: Snap Aggression
entries: If you are surprised at the start of combat and aren't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force to act normally on your first turn.

entries.name: Assertive Defense
entries: When you reduce the damage dealt by a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} to 0 using the {@i saber reflect} power, and you're wielding a {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} or {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force to reflect the attack at a target within range, regardless of what type the damage is.

subclassFeature.name: Fury
entries: You gain one of the following features. Choose Relentless for Juyo or Punishing {@optfeature Charge|sw5e-phb} for Vaapad.

entries.name: Relentless
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks, and gain a 10 foot bonus to your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} on your first turn of combat.

entries.name: Punishing Charge
entries: When a hostile creature you can see or hear within 30 feet of you casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. You must end this move closer to the enemy than you started. If you end this movement within 5 feet of the creature, and the triggering {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} required a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, they have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Vengeance
entries: You gain one of the following features. Choose Devastating Critical for Juyo or Their Power, My Strength for Vaapad.

entries.name: Devastating Critical
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you gain a bonus to that weapon's damage roll equal to your guardian level.

entries.name: Their Power, My Strength
entries: When you are dealt damage by a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can reduce that damage by an amount equal to your guardian level (no action required).
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Ferocity
entries: You are a paragon of extraordinary martial prowess. Your Strength and Dexterity scores increase by 2. Your maximum for those scores increases by 2. Additionally, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to all damage.
When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as part of that action.
Your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with weapons increases by 1.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Kage Order
entries: Monks of the Kage Order, known as Kage warriors, have mastered fighting in {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}, using that which others fear as a weapon against them. Kage warriors learn tricks to create {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness} where none exists, fighting using their intuition rather than relying on sight.

subclassFeature.name: Darkness Charges
entries: You learn to create a number of small charges that create enhanced {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}. Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can create two charges. You can create an additional {@optfeature Charge|sw5e-phb|charge} at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. Your charges can only be used by you, and they lose their potency at the end of your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Once per turn, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} or unarmed strike, you can instead throw one of your charges. Your charges have a range equal to 30 feet + your Strength modifier x 5. You can throw a device at a point you can see within range. The charges create a pocket of {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness} in a 10-foot radius sphere centered on that point. The {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness} spreads around corners. It lasts for 1 minute or until an enhanced source of bright light dispells it.

It lasts for 1 minute or until an enhanced source of bright light dispells it.

subclassFeature.name: Disruptive Shock
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} when you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, or it fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect that you control, you can choose to roll a Martial Arts die and deal additional psychic damage equal to the amount rolled.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain any expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: One With Darkness
entries: You have learned to become one with the shadows. When you are in an area of dim light or {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}, you can use your action to become {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible}. You remain {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} until you make an attack, cast a power, otherwise take a hostile action, or are in an area of bright light.

subclassFeature.name: Opportunist
entries: You can exploit a creature's momentary distraction when it is hit by an attack. Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a melee attack against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Kro Var Order
entries: Monks of the Kro Var Order—known as shapers—utilize a unique power to bend the four elements to their will, creating effects as small as a floating flame to quakes that sunder the earth.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Attunement
entries: You gain the ability to bend the elements to your will. As an action, you can manipulate these forces to create one of the following effects of your choice at a space within 10 feet of you:

items: Create a harmless, instantaneous sensory effect related to air, earth, fire, or water, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, a spray of light mist, or a gentle rumbling of stone.
Instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.
Chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material for up to 1 hour.
Cause earth, fire, water, or mist that can fit within a 1-foot cube to shape itself into a crude form you designate for 1 minute.

entries: This range increases to 30 feet at 11th level and 60 feet at 17th level.

Additionally, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can spend 1 focus point to conjure a weapon made of one of the four elements—air, earth, fire, or water—which lasts for 1 minute. Your weapon takes an appearance of your choice, it can only be used by you, and you can't be disarmed of it while you are conscious. You are proficient in this weapon, which counts as a monk weapon for you and uses your Martial Arts die for its damage rolls. You can only have one of these weapons at a time, and if you summon a new one the old one immediately disappears.

entries.name: Air
entries: Your whistling weapon has the returning property, the thrown property with a range of 20/60, and deals sonic damage on a hit. Additionally, when you hit a creature with the weapon, it is {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Earth
entries: Your earthen weapon takes the form of stone, and deals kinetic damage on a hit. Additionally, when you hit a creature with it, you can force the target to make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target is pushed back 5 feet. Lastly, while active, you can use Strength instead of Dexterity when determining your AC, as long as it doesn't already include that modifier.

entries.name: Fire
entries: Your flaming weapon sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet, deals fire damage, and when you hit a creature with it, the creature takes additional damage equal to half your focus ability modifier (minimum of one).

entries.name: Water
entries: Your watery weapon has the reach property, deals cold damage on a hit, and you can use your focus ability modifier instead of Dexterity or Strength for its attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can instead use your weapon to wet a 5-foot square within your weapon's reach. The affected area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}. Each creature who starts its turn in the square or enters it for the first time must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, falling {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone} on a failed save.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Adept
entries: You gain two of the following features. You gain an additional option at 11th and 17th level.

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 2 focus points to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 2 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Burning Ember Flourish
entries: You can use your action to choose an area of flame that you can see and that fits within a 5-foot cube within 60 feet. You can {@spell Extinguish|sw5e-phb|extinguish} the fire in that area, and you create either fireworks or smoke when you do so.

{@b {@i Fireworks.}} The target explodes with a dazzling display of colors. Each creature within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

{@b {@i Smoke.}} Thick black smoke spreads out from the target in a 20-foot radius, moving around corners. The area of the smoke is heavily obscured. The smoke persists for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it.

entries.name: Curtain of Unyielding Wind
entries: As an action, you call up a mighty gale, which swirls around you in a 10-foot radius and moves with you, remaining centered on you. The wind lasts for 10 minutes. The wind deafens both you and other creatures in its area. It extinguishes unprotected flames in its area that are torch-sized or smaller and hedges out vapor, gas, and fog that can be dispersed by strong wind. The area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for creatures other than you and the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} of ranged weapon attacks have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} if the attacks pass in or out of the wind.

entries.name: Crushing Hand of the Mountain
entries: As an action, you can choose a 5-foot-square unoccupied space on the ground that you can see within 30 feet. A Medium hand made from soil and stone, which lasts for 1 minute, rises in that space and reaches for one Large or smaller creature you can see within 5 feet of it. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 kinetic damage and is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} for the duration. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns, you can cause the hand to crush the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target, which must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. It takes 2d6 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. To break out, the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your focus save DC. On a success, the target escapes and is no longer {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} by the hand. As an action, you can cause the hand to reach for a different creature or to move to a different unoccupied space within range. The hand releases a {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target if you do either.

entries.name: Hatchling's Flame
entries: As an action, you focus your energy into a torrent of fire that streaks away from you. A line of roaring flame 30 feet long and 5 feet wide emanates from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Patient Bantha Listens
entries: You reach out to the ground beneath you. You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to gain {@sense Tremorsense|sw5e-phb|tremorsense} with a range of 30 feet and a burrow {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for up to 1 minute. Your movement leaves behind a tunnel that remains for as long as this ability is active, after which it collapses.

entries.name: Rush of the Shyrack
entries: As an action, you form a line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide that blasts from you in a direction you choose for one minute or until you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} or dismiss the effect (no action required). Each Large or smaller creature that starts its turn in the line must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be pushed 15 feet away from you in a direction following the line. Any creature in the line must spend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving closer to you. The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extinguishes candles, torches, and similar unprotected flames in the area. It causes protected flames, such as those of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent chance to {@spell Extinguish|sw5e-phb|extinguish} them. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns before the effect ends, you can change the direction in which the line blasts from you.

entries.name: Shape the Raincloud
entries: You can use your action pull water from air, and return it to the atmosphere. In an open container, you can create up to 20 gallons of drinkable water. You may also produce a rain that falls within a 30-foot cube and extinguishes open-air flames. You can destroy the same amount of water in an open container, or destroy a 30-foot cube of fog.

entries.name: Swarming Ice Rabbit
entries: As an action, you can cause a flurry of ice crystals to erupt from a point you can see within 90 feet. Each creature in a 5-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 cold damage, and gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed}.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Adept
entries: You gain two of the following features. You gain an additional option at 11th and 17th level.

You can use these features a combined number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the monk table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can instead expend 2 focus points to use it. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 2 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Burning Ember Flourish
entries: You can use your action to choose an area of flame that you can see and that fits within a 5-foot cube within 60 feet. You can {@spell Extinguish|sw5e-phb|extinguish} the fire in that area, and you create either fireworks or smoke when you do so.

{@b {@i Fireworks.}} The target explodes with a dazzling display of colors. Each creature within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or become {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

{@b {@i Smoke.}} Thick black smoke spreads out from the target in a 20-foot radius, moving around corners. The area of the smoke is heavily obscured. The smoke persists for 1 minute or until a strong wind disperses it.

entries.name: Curtain of Unyielding Wind
entries: As an action, you call up a mighty gale, which swirls around you in a 10-foot radius and moves with you, remaining centered on you. The wind lasts for 10 minutes. The wind deafens both you and other creatures in its area. It extinguishes unprotected flames in its area that are torch-sized or smaller and hedges out vapor, gas, and fog that can be dispersed by strong wind. The area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for creatures other than you and the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} of ranged weapon attacks have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} if the attacks pass in or out of the wind.

entries.name: Crushing Hand of the Mountain
entries: As an action, you can choose a 5-foot-square unoccupied space on the ground that you can see within 30 feet. A Medium hand made from soil and stone, which lasts for 1 minute, rises in that space and reaches for one Large or smaller creature you can see within 5 feet of it. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 kinetic damage and is {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} for the duration. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns, you can cause the hand to crush the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target, which must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. It takes 2d6 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. To break out, the {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} creature can use its action to make a Strength check against your focus save DC. On a success, the target escapes and is no longer {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} by the hand. As an action, you can cause the hand to reach for a different creature or to move to a different unoccupied space within range. The hand releases a {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained} target if you do either.

entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Crushing Hand of the Mountain} or {@i Patient Bantha Listens} As an action, you can choose a point you can see on the ground within 120 feet. entries.name: Ride the Wind
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Curtain of Unyielding Wind} or {@i Rush of the Shyrack} As an action, you can gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for 10 minutes. entries.name: River of Hungry Flame
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Burning Ember {@optfeature Flourish|sw5e-phb}} or {@i Hatchling's Flame} As an action, you can create a wall of fire on a solid surface within 120 feet. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and lasts for 1 minute.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 fire damage, or half as much damage on a successful save.

One side of the wall, chosen by you when you use this feature, deals 5d8 fire damage to each creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side of the wall. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The other side of the wall deals no damage.

entries.name: Shape the Flowing River
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Shape the Rainclud} or {@i Swarming Ice Rabbit} As an action, you can control any freestanding water within 300 feet of you inside an area you choose that is a cube up to 100 feet on a side. You can choose from any of the following effects when you use this feature. As an action on your turn, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

{@b {@i Flood.}} You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller creatures in the wave's path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller creatures struck by the wave have a 25 percent chance of being knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}. The water level remains elevated until the feature ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

{@b {@i Part Water.}} You cause water in the area to move apart and create a trench. The trench extends across the feature's area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the feature ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

{@b {@i Redirect Flow.}} You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the feature's area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain conditions. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the feature ends or you choose a different effect.

{@b {@i Whirlpool.}} This effect requires a body of water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature or object in the water and within 25 feet of the vortex is pulled 10 feet toward it. A creature can swim away from the vortex by making a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check against your feature save DC. When a creature enters the vortex for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 kinetic damage and is caught in the vortex until the feature ends. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, and isn't caught in the vortex. A creature caught in the vortex can use its action to try to swim away from the vortex as described above, but has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to do so. The first time each turn that an object enters the vortex, the object takes 2d8 kinetic damage; this damage occurs each round it remains in the vortex.

The ground in a 10-foot radius around you is icy and is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} for creatures other than you. The radius moves with you.

You can use your action to create a 15-foot cone of freezing ice extending from your outstretched hand in a direction you choose. Each creature in the cone must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 4d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save against this effect gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

entries.name: Embodiment of Earth
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Earth Reaches for Sky} As an action, you cause rock to envelop you, granting the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic and energy damage.

You can move across {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} made of earth or stone without spending extra movement. You can move through solid earth or stone as if it was air without destabilizing it, but you can't end your movement there. If you do so, you are immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space that you can occupy and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you are moved.

You can use your action to create a small {@spell Earthquake|sw5e-phb|earthquake} on the ground in a 15-foot radius centered on you. Other creatures on that ground must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to extend the benefits of this feature until the start of your next turn, to a maximum duration of 1 minute. This effect ends immediately if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die.

subclassFeature.name: Avatar
entries: As an ultimate display of your mastery of the elements, you can spend 5 focus points as an action to have the elements of water, earth, fire, and air form a protective sphere around your body, gaining multiple benefits for 1 minute. While this ability is active, you have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to cold, energy, fire, kinetic, lightning, and sonic damage. You also gain a burrow, fly, and swim {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. Lastly, you can use any of the following abilities as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}:

items: You create a small {@spell Earthquake|sw5e-phb|earthquake} on the ground in a 15-foot radius around you. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d6 kinetic damage and is knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

You create a line of fire 15 feet long and 5 feet wide extending from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

You create a 15-foot cube of swirling wind centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 1d10 kinetic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If a Large or smaller creature fails the save, that creature is also pushed up to 10 feet away from the center of the cube.

You create a 15-foot cone of ice shards extending from your outstretched hand in a direction you choose. Each creature in the cone must make a Constitution save throw. A creature takes 2d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save against this effect has its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} halved until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Kyuzo Order
entries: Monks of the Kyuzo Order turn weapon throwing into a true art form. Inspired by the skill of native kyuzo wielding their war helmets as both {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} and weapon, these monks utilize any thrown object they can find to defend themselves and others while they attack enemies from angles both surprising and devastating.

subclassFeature.name: Intercept
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} with the thrown property and they become monk weapons for you. Additionally, when you throw an improvised weapon, you are considered proficient in it, and it uses your Martial Arts die instead of its 1d4.

Additionally, you've learned to use thrown weapons to intercept projectiles traveling towards your allies. When you are wielding a weapon with which you are proficient, and a creature within your weapon's normal thrown range is hit by a ranged attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to throw your weapon to intercept the projectile. When you do so, the damage the creature takes from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level. If the weapon has the returning property, it then returns to your hand.

subclassFeature.name: Scattering Stance
entries: When you take the {@action Dodge|sw5e-phb} action, until the start of your next turn you gain a number of special reactions equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} that you can only use for your Intercept feature. You can only take one {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Curved Throw
entries: You can curve your throws behind {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}. When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with a weapon with the thrown property, you can spend 1 focus point to cause the target to gain no benefit from {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} or {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, unless that {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} is full {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

subclassFeature.name: Relentless Assault
entries: When you make multiple weapon attacks with thrown weapons against the same target on your turn, each attack after the first gains a +1 bonus to its {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, cumulatively, to a maximum bonus of +6.

subclassFeature.name: Mastermind Technique
entries: Preparation, preparation, preparation. Some scouts are serious students of battle and any creatures they might encounter. Followers of the Mastermind Technique focus on being prepared for any eventuality, and using their breadth of knowledge to gain insights into their enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Instinctive Combatant
entries: You have learned to use your wits to help you {@optfeature Survive|sw5e-phb|survive}. While you are wearing light or {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier when determining your AC.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Meticulous
entries: You can use Intelligence instead of Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls made with weapons with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} or {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons against the target of your Ranger's Quarry.

Additionally, once per round, when you hit the target of your Ranger's Quarry with a tech attack, or it fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that deals damage, you can deal additional damage equal to your Ranger's Quarry damage die of the same type as the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}'s damage.

subclassFeature.name: Adaptive Techie
entries: When you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can choose up to a number of {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you know equal to half your Intelligence modifier and replace them with another {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, as long as that power is not of a higher level than your Max Power Level.

subclassFeature.name: Emergency Planning
entries: You've learned to formulate and execute a plan. As an action, you can choose up to six creatures (including yourself) that you can see within 60 feet of you. For each creature, choose one of the following: {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Each creature gains an Emergency Planning die, which is a {@dice d8}.

Once within the next 10 minutes, each creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, as determined when you use this feature. The creature can wait until after it rolls the {@dice d20} before deciding to use the Emergency Planning die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Emergency Planning die is rolled, it is lost.
A creature can have only one Emergency Planning die at a time.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.
Your Emergency Planning die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Exploit Weakness
entries: Your training has taught you to find and exploit weaknesses in your prey. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} the target of your Ranger's Quarry makes against an effect you control before the end of your next turn. Once you've done so, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can do so again.

subclassFeature.name: Maverick Practice
entries: There are those who, when thrust into danger, use unexpected methods to achieve victory. Those operatives who choose the Maverick Practice draw on a wide array of skills, learning new ways to apply them, as their strongest asset.

subclassFeature.name: Maverick Superiority
entries: You learn {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers Known
entries: You learn two {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} of your choice, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the Maverick Superiority table. Many {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} per attack, and you may only use each {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} once per turn.
Each time you learn new {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}, you can also replace one {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Quantity column of the Maverick Superiority table. This die changes as you gain operative levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Size column of the Maverick Superiority table. A superiority die is expended when you use it.
You regain all of your expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use. You use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (your choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (your choice), and an ability of your choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. You use this ability whenever a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} refers to your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

subclassFeature.name: Know a Bit
entries: You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} you make that doesn't already include your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeature.name: Outplayed
entries: When a creature fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} against you or an effect you control, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use Sneak Attack, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature, and that creature can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects you control. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Practice Makes Perfect
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} as part of or that is affected by a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use, you can choose to increase your level of proficiency in that check by one step (from trained to proficient, from proficient to {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}, from {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} to mastery, from mastery to high mastery, or from high mastery to grand mastery).
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Practice Makes Perfect
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} as part of or that is affected by a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use, you can choose to increase your level of proficiency in that check by one step (from trained to proficient, from proficient to {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}, from {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} to mastery, from mastery to high mastery, or from high mastery to grand mastery).
You can use this feature five times. You gain an additional use at 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Flow State
entries: As an action, you can choose to intensely focus for one minute, gaining the following benefits:

items: Once on each of your turns, when you use a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}, you can use a {@dice d4} instead of expending a superiority die.
You can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
Creatures can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you.

entries: Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Mechanist Technique
entries: Some scouts are peerless inventors, skilled at working with droids and other forms of technology. Followers of the Mechanist Technique make up for the weakness of organics with the strength and purity of their creations.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Techcasting
entries: Your command of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} improves.

entries.name: Improved Tech Powers Known
entries: You know 7 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, instead of 5, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Improved Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to one and a half times your scout level, instead of your scout level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Improved Max Power Level
entries: Your Max Power Level becomes 2nd, instead of 1st, and it increases at higher levels, as shown in the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.

You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th, 6th, and 7th-level once, instead of 4th and 5th. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Mechanist
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can cause the target of your Ranger's Quarry to emit an ion pulse, as long as the target is within 60 feet of you. The target, and any creatures within 5 feet of it, must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, roll your Ranger's Quarry die; each creature takes ion damage equal to the amount rolled.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Tech
entries: You can use your ingenuity to bolster yourself or an ally. As an action, you can touch one creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits of your choice to that creature:

items: For 10 minutes, the creature can roll a d3 whenever making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} and add the number rolled to the {@dice d20} roll. Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Roll a {@dice d4}. The creature regains a number of tech points equal to the result. Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries: You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Roll a {@dice d4}. The creature regains a number of tech points equal to the result. Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: High Voltage
entries: You are used to working with electronics and have learned to increase their potency, while becoming inured to their dangers. You gain {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to ion and lightning damage.

Additionally, whenever you deal ion damage to a creature, you can spend a tech point to force the creature to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Command Droid
entries: You can reprogram a droid and bring it under your control. As an action, you can touch one droid that you can see that is the target of your Ranger's Quarry. That creature must make a Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. If it succeeds, you can't use this feature on it again for 24 hours. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.

Intelligent droids are harder to control in this way. If the target has an Intelligence of 8 or higher, it has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and has an Intelligence of 12 or higher, it can repeat the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

subclassFeature.name: Mechanist Technique (Companion)
entries: Some scouts are peerless inventors, skilled at working with droids and other forms of technology. Followers of the Mechanist Technique utilize the assistance of a tracker droid companion to make up for the weakness of organics with the strength and purity of their creations.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Techcasting
entries: Your command of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} improves.

entries.name: Improved Tech Powers Known
entries: You know 7 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, instead of 5, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Improved Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to one and a half times your scout level, instead of your scout level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Improved Max Power Level
entries: Your Max Power Level becomes 2nd, instead of 1st, and it increases at higher levels, as shown in the Mechanist Technique {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.

You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th, 6th, and 7th-level once, instead of 4th and 5th. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Tracker Droid Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to create and customize your own tracker droid companion.

Create your tracker droid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements} in order to create your droid.
In addition to its traits and features, your tracker droid companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your tracker droid gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each droid trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of droid traits equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).

entries: Lastly, while your tracker droid companion is bonded and within 10 feet of you, you can use your action to learn the location of any droid or construct, tech focus, {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or enhanced item within 60 feet of you or your tracker droid that isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|total cover}. When you sense a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} in this way, you learn what the power is. At 11th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 30 feet of you or your target to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 60 feet. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Tracker Droid Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to create and customize your own tracker droid companion.

Create your tracker droid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements} in order to create your droid.
In addition to its traits and features, your tracker droid companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your tracker droid gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each droid trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1.
