subclassFeature.name: Performance Practice
entries: Some operatives choose to master finesse and timing through performance art. Those operatives who choose the {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb} Practice become skilled performers who prove especially deadly in close combat, able to find the rhythm of an attacker's strikes as easily as any song.

subclassFeature.name: Artful Dancer
entries: Your training with music and dancing grants you certain benefits. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb} skill and one musical instrument of your choice.

Additionally, while you are not wearing armor or wielding a medium or heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, you can add half your Charisma modifier to your AC as long as it doesn't already include that modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Dazzling Steps
entries: You learn to conduct impressive displays of grace and {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in combat. While you aren't wearing medium or {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor} or wielding a medium or heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, and you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn and attack with a weapon with either the light or finesse properties, your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn, and if you deal Sneak Attack damage, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a dazzling step.

Some of your dazzling steps require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the dazzling step's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Dazzling Step save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier

entries.name: Defensive Step
entries: You defend yourself from further attack. Roll two Sneak Attack dice. You gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} that last until the start of your next turn equal to the amount rolled.

entries.name: Mobile Step
entries: You twist and twirl around the target. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A Huge or larger creature automatically succeeds. On a failed save, it is pushed back 5 feet, and you can immediately move into the space it just vacated without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

entries.name: Offensive Step
entries: Choose another creature that you can see within your reach. The creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, roll two Sneak Attack dice. The creature takes damage equal to the amount rolled. This damage is of the same as your weapon's damage.

subclassFeature.name: Flexible Body
entries: You are able to use your acrobatic talent to gain the upper hand in combat. You can use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} granted by your Cunning Action to shove or trip a creature. When you do so, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) check instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check.

Additionally, you now ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, you can move through space occupied by hostile creatures, and you can squeeze through smaller spaces without expending extra movement.

subclassFeature.name: Dance of Death
entries: You can use your action to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for each target. You can choose to deal Sneak Attack damage to each creature you hit, but you can only roll half your number of Sneak Attack dice per creature.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Dance
entries: Your confidence when putting on a show has extended into combat. You add your Charisma modifier to {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks. Additionally, any creature who fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your Dazzling Step save DC has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} they make against you each turn until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Praetorian Specialist
entries: Those fighters who choose to become Praetorian Specialists seek perfection of both body and mind. These warriors master the art of warfare, and are often sought as bodyguards for the galaxy's elite. They are engines of destruction and resilience, able to fight on to their last breath.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Performance|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Fighting Spirit
entries: Your intensity in battle can {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} you and help you strike true. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on all {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack rolls} until the end of the current turn. When you do so, you also gain 5 temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. The number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 10 at 10th level and 15 at 15th level.
You can use this feature three times. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Resilient Retainer
entries: Your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations. You gain proficiency in {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}.

Additionally, your self-control also causes you to gain proficiency in Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Tireless Spirit
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} and have no uses of Fighting Spirit remaining, you regain one use.

subclassFeature.name: Rapid Strike
entries: You learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn and have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against one of the targets, you can forgo the {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} for that roll to make an additional {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Strength Before Weakness
entries: Your fighting spirit can delay the grasp of death. If you take damage that reduces you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to delay falling {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious}, and you can immediately take an extra turn. While you have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} during that extra turn, taking damage causes {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} failures as normal, and three {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throw} failures can still kill you. When the extra turn ends, you fall {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious} if you still have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Precision Approach
entries: Some berserkers have learned to channel their rage into a method of increasing their focus and precision to supernatural levels. Those berserkers who choose the Precision Approach hone their rage to a fine point, becoming agile warriors who ruthlessly dispatch their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Careful Steps
entries: You gain skills that represent your precise movement. You gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}. While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on checks you make with the chosen skill.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Rage
entries: You hone your rage to a razor sharp focus. While raging, when you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} using Dexterity, you add your rage damage to the damage roll. Additionally, you can use your Reckless Attack feature to give you {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on melee weapon attacks using Dexterity during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Anticipation
entries: While raging, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with melee weapon attacks using Dexterity increases by 1.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Danger Sense
entries: While raging, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage against effects that you can see, such as traps and powers, you are treated as proficient in the save, and you instead take no damage if you succeed on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if you fail.

subclassFeature.name: Calm Within the Storm
entries: The precision with which you act during your rage causes you to become a storm of reactive lethality. When you use your Reckless Attack feature, you can make a number of {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} without using your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}, and when a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} using Dexterity against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Predator Technique
entries: Some scouts work in solitude, while others prefer the strength of a group. Followers of the Predator Technique find power lies with the pack; they distract their prey, while their allies go for the kill.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Party
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Party
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Party
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Party
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Hunting Party
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Predator
entries: If the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature can see you, a number of friendly creatures you choose up to your Intelligence modifier have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made to hide from it.

subclassFeature.name: Predator's Resolve
entries: You can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.
At the start of each of your turns, you gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one).
When you use your Hunting Party feature and the target of the attack is your Ranger's Quarry, your ally gains a bonus to damage on the attack equal to your Ranger's Quarry Damage Die.

entries: Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Prey on the Weak
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, and the creature is below its hit point maximum, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against that creature before the end of your next turn by someone other than you has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

subclassFeature.name: On the Hunt
entries: When you use your Predator's Resolve feature, a number of friendly creatures you choose up to your Intelligence modifier that you can see within 30 feet of you also gain the benefits of the feature.

subclassFeature.name: Pugnacity Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Pugnacity Practice apply an atypical versatility to their actions, comfortably dispatching foes from afar or face to face.

subclassFeature.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You've learned to move swiftly while wielding larger armaments. You gain proficiency with {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor} and martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}. If you are already proficient in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you instead gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}. Additionally, you can deal Sneak Attack damage with any weapon, as long as it does not have the heavy or special properties.

Lastly, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if no creature other than your target is within 5 feet of you, as long as the target of the attack is below its hit point maximum. All the other rules for the Sneak Attack class feature still apply to you.

subclassFeature.name: Blitz Attack
entries: You've learned ways to use your martial ability to boost your combat performance. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a blitz attack.

Some of your blitz attacks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the attack's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is as follows:
{@b Blitz Attack save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

entries.name: Demoralizing Attack
entries: The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it is {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Diverting Attack
entries: Roll two of your Sneak Attack dice. The first time the target would deal damage before the start of your next turn, that damage is reduced by an amount equal to the resulting roll.

entries.name: Warmonger's Attack
entries: If the target makes an attack against you or an allied creature within 5 feet of you before the start of your next turn, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against it.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn, you can choose to attack twice, instead of once. Additionally, you can deal Sneak Attack damage any number of times on your turn. Each time you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can choose how many Sneak Attack dice you apply. You can't apply more than your total Sneak Attack dice each turn.

subclassFeature.name: Unrelenting Advance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would grapple or restrain you. Additionally, if you are {@condition Grappled|sw5e-phb|grappled} or {@condition Restrained|sw5e-phb|restrained}, and you could use your action to attempt to end the effect, you can instead use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Razor Focus
entries: You can enter a hyper-focused state of mind for 1 minute as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. You must maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, as if concentrating on a power. For the duration, each time you successfully deal Sneak Attack damage against a creature, you gain two additional Sneak Attack dice, cumulatively, as your attacks become increasingly precise. These additional dice are lost when your focus ends, whether through failing to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} or after 1 minute.

The first time you use this feature, you suffer no ill effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you suffer one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} each time you use it.

subclassFeature.name: Rakatan Order
entries: Monks of the Rakatan Order believe in the harmony of self with technology. They use tech to push themselves beyond their body's natural limits.

subclassFeature.name: Techcasting
entries: You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your monk level (rounded up), as shown in the Tech Points column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice). You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Rakatan Order {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} (your choice). You use this ability whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifer
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifer

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}) as a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Tech
entries: You can cast your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} using your focus points. When you do so, your maximum focus points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
Additionally, when you use a Focus feature, you gain the following tech enhancements. Each effect costs 1 tech point.
{@b {@i Flurry of Blows.}} When you hit with an attack with Flurry of Blows, you can deal an additional 1d8 damage of the same type.

entries.name: Rakatan Techcasting
entries: {@b {@i Patient Defense.}} While under the effects of your Patient Defense, when you are hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll your Martial Arts die to increase your AC against the attack.

{@b {@i Step of the Wind.}} While under the effects of your Step of the Wind, you can become immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition, and have each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.

subclassFeature.name: Harmonious Rakatan
entries: You can use your Focus features using your tech points. When you do so, your maximum tech points are reduced by 1 until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Additionally, you are constantly under the effects of the {@i detect enhancement} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. As an action, you can cast the {@i analyze} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} without expending tech points. When you do so, {@i detect enhancement} is suppressed and you can't do so again until you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Tech Mastery
entries: You learn and can cast one 5th-level {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} without expending tech points.

subclassFeature.name: Ruffian Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Ruffian Practice use rough-and-{@optfeature Tumble|sw5e-phb|tumble} tactics to handle any fight, big or small. They {@optfeature Incite|sw5e-phb|incite} chaos and make devious moves that keep their enemies reeling.

subclassFeature.name: Rakish Audacity
entries: Your unmistakable confidence propels you into battle. You can add your Charisma modifier to your {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} rolls.

Additionally, you don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if no creature other than your target is within 5 feet of you, as long as the target of the attack is within 5 feet of you. All the other rules for the Sneak Attack class feature still apply to you.
Finally, during your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you for the rest of your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Nimble Step
entries: You learn to fluidly strike and {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} through combat. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} across the battlefield.

Some of your fancy footworks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the debilitating strike's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Nimble Step save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Blade Defense
entries: You attempt to determine your target's next strike. Roll two Sneak Attack dice, and the target must make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, your AC increases by the higher amount rolled on the dice against the first attack it makes against you before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, your AC instead increases by the lower amount.

entries.name: Disarming Strike
entries: You attempt to disarm a creature with your attack. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be forced to drop one item of your choice that it's holding. If you have a free hand, you can catch the item. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.

entries.name: Fancy Footwork
entries: Roll two Sneak Attack dice. Your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 5 x the greater result of the two dice, and you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until the end of your current turn.

subclassFeature.name: Panache
entries: Your charm becomes extraordinarily beguiling. As an action, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check contested by a creature's Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check. The creature must be able to hear you, and the two of you must share a language.

If you succeed on the check and the creature is hostile to you, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against targets other than you and can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against targets other than you. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until one of your companions attacks the target or affects it with a power, or until you and the target are more than 60 feet apart.

If you succeed on the check and the creature isn't hostile to you, it is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you for 1 minute. While {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed}, it regards you as a friendly acquaintance. This effect ends immediately if you or your companions do anything harmful to it.

subclassFeature.name: Elegant Maneuver
entries: You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|sw5e-phb}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check you make during the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Master Duelist
entries: Your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat. If you miss with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can roll it again with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. Once you do so, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Saboteur Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Saboteur Practice enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with tech, using advanced technology with the aid of a tracker droid to sustain a longer assault.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}.

subclassFeature.name: Techcasting
entries: You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your operative level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Saboteur Practice {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}) as a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

subclassFeature.name: Tracker Droid Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to create and customize your own tracker droid companion.

Create your tracker droid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. You must have {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements} in order to create your droid.
In addition to its traits and features, your tracker droid companion gains an additional benefit while it is bonded to you:

items: Your tracker droid gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each droid trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your tech point maximum is reduced by 1. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can install, replace, or remove a number of tracker droid traits equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).

entries: Lastly, when you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st-level or higher that would affect only one target, and your tracker droid companion is bonded and within 10 feet of you or your target, your tracker droid companion can use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to increase the level at which you are casting your power by 1. This feature can increase a power's level above your Max Power Level, and using this feature does not cost additional tech points.
At 11th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 30 feet of you or your target to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your tracker droid companion must be within 60 feet.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Powered Ambush
entries: If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a power on it, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on any {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes against the power this turn.

subclassFeature.name: Ion Pulse
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can expend one or more of your tracker droid's Hit Dice to have it emit an pulse of ion energy. Each creature within 5 feet of your tracker droid must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. A creature takes ion damage for each Hit Die expended in this way on a failed save, or half as much as on a successful one. The size of the damage die equals the size of your tracker droid's Hit Die. Any electronics not being worn or carried within the blast radius are disabled until rebooted.

subclassFeature.name: Sabotage
entries: You gain the ability to sabotage a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} in the process of being cast. When a hostile creature casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, and you are the target of the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} or within its area of effect, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force that creature to make an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a successful save, the power is cast as normal.

On a failed save, you negate the power's effects, and the caster takes 1d6 lightning damage per level of the power it was casting. Additionally, on a failed save, the caster's tech focus used to cast the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} is overloaded and can't be used to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for 1 minute.

At the end of each of the caster's turns, it can repeat the Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a success, it can use the tech focus to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} again.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Sawbones Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Sawbones Practice have studied the humanoid body on a more intimate level than other operatives. While others may know where best to stab in order to kill, you also know how to repair the wounds you inflict, as well as how to make them even deeper. You delve into the secrets of the body, learning as much medical knowledge as you can get your hands on, regardless of how dirty the work becomes.

subclassFeature.name: General Practice
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb}, and you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Wisdom modifier for checks made with it.

Additionally, you can expend one use of a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} to help {@spell Revitalize|sw5e-phb|revitalize} your wounded allies during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}. If you or any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} at the end of the {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
The extra {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Debilitating Strike
entries: You learn to apply your anatomical knowledge in direct combat, in order to hinder your targets. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to hinder the creature, provided they have the appropiate physiology.

Some of your debilitating strikes require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the debilitating strike's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Debilitating Strike save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Bleeding Wound
entries: You attempt to create a lingering wound in the target for one minute. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, at the start of each of the target's turns, it takes true damage equal to one Sneak Attack die and repeats this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Crippling Pain
entries: You attempt to cause distracting pain in the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hampering Shot
entries: You attempt to hamper the target's movement. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and it makes Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Swift Surgery
entries: You know how to quickly patch up wounds, given the right tools. You are able to use a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} or administer a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, and when you use a {@item Traumakit|sw5e-phb|traumakit} to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Dosage Control
entries: Your knowledge of medicine allows you to partition and ration healing supplies very effectively, without impacting its potency. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a rest, you can carefully measure and mark out dosages of a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} within reach. The {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} can now be used twice before it is consumed.
At your DM's discretion, you may be able to use this feature on other pacs, stims, or adrenals, most likely involving an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} to succeed.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Sustain
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}.
Additionally, when you are stabilized, you regain 1 hit point. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Scrapper Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Scrapper Practice don't have the time or patience for the fair fight. They utilize close-quarters {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} combat blended with underhanded tactics to surprise and disable their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Back Blast
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true} with the burst or rapid property that lack the two-handed property. Additionally, when a creature fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the burst or rapid property of a weapon you control and with which you are proficient, you can apply your Sneak Attack damage to one creature dealt damage in this way as long as that creature didn't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save.

When you reach 9th level in this class, when multiple creatures fail a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the burst property of a weapon you control and with which you are proficient, you can divide your Sneak Attack dice amongst the targets as you see fit.

subclassFeature.name: Upper Hand
entries: You learn to use underhanded tactics to gain the upper hand. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack Dice in order to perform an upper hand technique.

Some of your upper hand techniques require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the technique's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Upper Hand save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier

entries.name: Brutal Hit
entries: You attempt to knock the target prone while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition Prone|sw5e-phb|prone}.

entries.name: Low Blow
entries: You attempt to stun the target while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Shank Shot
entries: You attempt to hamper the target while within 15 feet of it. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If it fails, it gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level and makes Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Sleight of Foot
entries: When a creature moves to within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} away from the creature without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. You must end this movement further from the creature than you started.

subclassFeature.name: Hostile Negotiations
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}. Additionally, while you are wielding a weapon with which you are proficient, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) checks, and if the target would make a contested check, they can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on it.

subclassFeature.name: Double Tap
entries: You can deal Sneak Attack damage twice per turn, but you can't deal more than your total Sneak Attack dice to a single target per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Killer Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Shadow Killer Practice are master assassins, the spiritual practitioners who combine their finely honed skills with mystical aid to vanish from sight and neutralize their targets with {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison}-coated weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Venomous
entries: You gain proficiency with the {@item Poisoner's kit|sw5e-phb|poisoner's kit}, and you can apply a {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

Additionally, you learn to create a number of special {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} vials. Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can create two doses of {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison}. You must have a {@item Poisoner's kit|sw5e-phb|poisoner's kit} in order to create these doses. Your doses can only be used by you, and they lose their potency at the end of your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

As an action, you can use one of your doses to coat one {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon}, one {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge}, or one {@item Wrist launcher|sw5e-phb|wrist launcher} dart. A creature hit by the coated weapon must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier), taking 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Once applied, the {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} retains potency for 1 minute before drying.
The quantity and damage of your doses increases at higher levels, to three and 2d4 at 5th level, four and 3d4 at 9th level, five and 4d4 at 13th level, and six and 5d4 at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Arts
entries: You learn to combine {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} and stealth to perform assassination techniques. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a dark art.
{@b Dark Arts save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Envenomed Art
entries: You attempt to {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} the target. The target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hallucinatory Art
entries: You attempt to blind the target. The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Vanishing Art
entries: You feint to momentarily disappear from your target's purview. The target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failure, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} from the target.

subclassFeature.name: Poisoner
entries: You are a master of poisons. Targets of your poisons cannot have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made to resist your {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight Of Hand|sw5e-phb}) checks made to {@optfeature Conceal|sw5e-phb|conceal} the application of poisons.

Additionally, when you apply {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} to a weapon or its ammunition, that {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} can affect an additional hit or an additional piece of ammunition, and when you deal Sneak Attack damage with an attack that would include {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage, you can change your Sneak Attack damage to {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage.

subclassFeature.name: One With the Dark
entries: You learn to partially enter the spirit realm. As an action, you can become {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} as an enhanced effect, along with anything you are wearing or carrying, for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. While you have no remaining uses of this feature, you can expend one of your {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} doses from your Venomous feature to use this feature again. When you do so, your maximum doses decreases by 1 until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Shades of Night
entries: Your familiarity with poisons and the spirit realm has opened up new paths of life and death for you. Your Evasion feature now applies to Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} as well as Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

Additionally, whenever you create {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} using your Venomous feature, you can change the damage type to acid, cold, fire, lightning or necrotic. When you do so, and you deal Sneak Attack damage with a weapon coated with your {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison}, you can also change your Sneak Attack damage to the chosen type.

subclassFeature.name: Shii-Cho Form
entries: {@optfeature Shii-Cho Form|sw5e-phb}, also known as Determination Form, uses wild, unpredictable attacks designed to distract and disarm their foes. Those guardians who focus on {@optfeature Shii-Cho Form|sw5e-phb} make seemingly random, yet deliberate, attacks to knock their opponents off-balance.

subclassFeature.name: Form Basics
entries: You gain the Shii-Cho {@book lightsaber form, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of the Player's Handbook. If you already know this form, you can instead choose another {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}.

subclassFeature.name: The Way of the Sarlaac
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can enter a frenetic stance for one minute. While in this stance, the first time you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} on your turn, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} it makes against you before the start of your next turn. Additionally, if that creature is within 5 feet of you, it must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, it is pushed back 5 feet, and you can immediately move into the space it just vacated without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You gain the following Channel the Force option.

entries.name: Disarming Slash
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force (no action required)  to attempt to disarm the target, forcing it to drop one item of your choice that it's holding. The creature must make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. On a failed save, it drops the object you choose. If you are within 5 feet of the target, and you have a free hand, you can catch the item. Otherwise, the object lands at its feet.

subclassFeature.name: Unpredictable Motion
entries: While you are wielding a light- or vibro-weapon, {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

subclassFeature.name: Sarlaac Sweep
entries: When a creature moves to within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against that creature. If the attack hits, you can attempt to damage another creature within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. If the original {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} would hit the second creature, it takes damage equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Determination
entries: The erratic fluidity of your movement confounds even the most determined of foes. Your Strength or Dexterity and Wisdom or Charisma scores (your choice) increase by 2. Your maximum for these scores increases by 2. Additionally, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic, energy, and ion damage from weapons.
Attack rolls made against you can't have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

When more than one creature is within 5 feet of you, you gain a bonus to your {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb} equal to the number of creatures within 5 feet of you, up to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

When you use your Sarlaac Sweep feature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, and you can apply the bonus damage to every creature within 5 feet of you.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Slicer Pursuit
entries: Across the galaxy one can find numerous pseudonyms and false identities belonging to the hackers and cyber-infiltrators that call the world of electronics home. Those scholars who choose the Slicer Pursuit put their impressive intellectual prowess to work in the field of technology, to ends both benevolent and malicious.

subclassFeature.name: Hacker's Disposition
entries: You gain proficiency with slicer's kits and in the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

subclassFeature.name: Techcasting
entries: You have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 3 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to half of your scholar level, as shown in the Tech Points column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the Slicer Pursuit {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 4th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5} of the Player's Handbook) as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

subclassFeature.name: Systems Hijack
entries: Also at 3rd level, when the target of your Critical Analysis is a droid or construct, or wearing or holding a {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} focus, that creature is a viable target for any {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} with you cast with a range of touch.

Additionally, when the target of your Critical Analysis casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to identify the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} being cast, and at what level.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Programming
entries: When a creature succeeds on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast that deals damage, the creature takes half the power's damage, but suffers no additional effects of the power.

subclassFeature.name: Redirect Error
entries: When the target of your Critical Analysis feature casts a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that affects an area, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to cause that power to instead affect an area in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the caster.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: System Override
entries: You know how to quickly activate anti-tech subroutines you have encoded into your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. You can cast the {@i diminish tech} and {@i tech override} powers at 3rd level without expending tech points. If the target is the target of your Critical Analysis, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} check for these powers.
You can use this feature three times. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Slicer Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your understanding of tech casting. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Administrator's Log
entries: If you spend at least 10 minutes working on a computer or terminal, you can get a full list of users who have accessed the machine within the past 24 hours. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you may then form a facsimile of identification that would allow you to pass yourself off as that person when accessing machines.

entries.name: Backdoor Egress
entries: When you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that affects an area and requires a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and you are inside that power's area, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. If you end this movement outside the area affected by the {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, you do not have to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to avoid its effects.

entries.name: Intelligence Core Override
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} You can cast the {@i override interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 5th level without spending tech points.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Resource Appropriation
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 11th level} If you reduce the target of your Critical Analysis feature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, and it has tech point remaining, you may choose to gain any tech points it had remaining. Your current tech points cannot exceed your tech point maximum.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Skillful Casting
entries: When you hit a creature with an at-will {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that requires an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you may treat that {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} as a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} for the purpose of using {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Sleeper Program
entries: Whenever you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} with a casting time of 1 action, you can choose to delay the power's activation up to a minute. When you do so, you cast the power as normal, but holds its energy for the duration of the delay. Holding onto the power's effect requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. If your {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} is broken before the delay ends, the power dissipates without taking effect. You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to activate the power at any time.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses  when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Sokan Form
entries: {@optfeature Sokan Form|sw5e-phb}, also known as Persistence Form, uses determined movements followed by swift strokes to keep their opponents' footing unsteady. Those guardians who focus on Persistence Form make use of the terrain, trying to {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} their opponents into vulnerable areas before dispatching them.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

subclassFeature.name: Form Basics
entries: You gain the Sokan {@book lightsaber form, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of the Player's Handbook. If you already know this form, you can instead choose another {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}.

subclassFeature.name: The Way of the Varactyl
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can enter an unyielding stance for one minute. While in this stance, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to shove, trip, and avoid being moved, and you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}. Additionally, once per turn, when you hit with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can attempt to shove the target up to 10 feet away from you (no action required).

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You gain the following Channel the Force option.

entries.name: High Ground Defense
entries: When an opponent within 5 feet of you makes a melee attack against you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a use of your Channel the Force to move to another space within 5 feet of that creature without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}, imposing {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the roll. If the attack misses, you can attempt to shove the creature up to 10 feet away from you as a part of that same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Unwavering Self
entries: If you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can reroll the die. You must use the new roll.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again. At 15th level you can use this feature twice between long rests.

subclassFeature.name: Unwavering Self
entries: If you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can reroll the die. You must use the new roll.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again. At 15th level you can use this feature twice between long rests.

subclassFeature.name: Unhindered Charge
entries: Wen you move at least 10 feet before making a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you deal additional damage equal to your Strength modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Persistence
entries: You are an unrelenting force on the field of battle. Your Strength and Wisdom or Charisma scores (your choice) increase by 2. Your maximum for these scores increases by 2. Additionally, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic, energy, and ion damage from weapons.
You ignore effects that would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

Once per turn, when you push a creature, you can move up to 10 feet as a part of this push without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. If you end this movement within 5 feet of that creature, you can make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} (no action required).

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Teleportation Technique
entries: Whether through experimentation or discovery of an ancient technology, followers of the Teleportation Technique have learned to create brief teleportation portals, allowing them to {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} and attack both quickly and unpredictably throughout the battlefield.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}.

subclassFeature.name: Personal Teleporter
entries: You can use portable teleporters as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, instead of an action.

Additionally, while you are wielding a tech focus, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to create a pair of linked portals: one portal appears in a space within 5 feet of you, and the other portal appears in an unoccupied space you can see up to 30 feet away. These portals last until the start of your next turn, and they are large enough to accommodate Medium and smaller creatures and objects. Portals take the appearance of an elongated, shimmering {@item Mirror|sw5e-phb|mirror}, and looking through a portal, a creature can see through the linked portal as if looking through a window. A creature or object who passes through a portal immediately appears in a space within 5 feet of the linked portal. You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to end your portals early. If a creature is partially within your portals, it is shunted back to the space it previously occupied and it must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your a tech save DC. On a failed save, it takes energy damage equal to your scout level + your Intelligence modifier. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. At the beginning of each of your turns while you have a pair of portals active, you can expend a use of this feature to extend the duration of the portals until the start of your next turn (no action required). The distance at which you can create portals increases at higher levels. It increases to 60 feet at 5th level, 90 feet at 9th level, 150 feet at 13th level, 300 feet at 17th level, and 1,000 feet at 20th level.
