subclassFeature.name: Visions of the Past
entries: You can call up visions of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute in meditation, then receive dreamlike, shadowy glimpses of recent events. You can meditate in this way for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score and must maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} during that time, as if you were casting a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@b {@i Object Reading.}} Holding an object as you meditate, you can see visions of the object's previous owner. After meditating for 1 minute, you learn how the owner acquired and lost the object, as well as the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If the object was owned by another creature in the recent past (within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score), you can spend 1 additional minute for each owner to learn the same information about that creature.

{@b {@i Area Reading.}} As you meditate, you see visions of recent events in your immediate vicinity (a room, street, tunnel, clearing, or the like, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. For each minute you meditate, you learn about one significant event, beginning with the most recent. Significant events typically involve powerful emotions, such as battles and betrayals, marriages and murders, births and funerals. However, they might also include more mundane events that are nevertheless important in your current situation.

subclassFeature.name: Shielded Thoughts
entries: Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it. You also have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage that you do.

subclassFeature.name: Clarity of Vision
entries: The visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more accurate picture in your mind of what is to come. You roll three d20s for your Force Visions feature, rather than two.

subclassFeature.name: Way of Tutelage
entries: With the Force, knowledge is most often passed from a master to an apprentice. Those consulars who follow the Way of Tutelage know the strength of working together exceeds that of working alone.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in your choice of {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Humanoid Companion
entries: You've taken an apprentice, gaining the services of your own humanoid companion.
Create your humanoid companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your companion gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your force point maximum is reduced by 2.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, when your companion is hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a use of your Force {@item Shield|sw5e-phb} feature to shroud it in Force energy. If you do so, until the start of your next turn, both you and your companion gain the benefits of your Force {@item Shield|sw5e-phb}. This includes the triggering attack.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Strength Flows from the Force
entries: When you cast a power that affects only your companion, you can choose to treat the power as if cast at your Max Power Level.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the consular table. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: You Have That Power Too
entries: The bond between you and your companion has strengthened. When your companion is within 10 feet of you, and either you or your companion casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that would affect only one of you, you can instead have it affect both.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: You Have That Power Too
entries: The bond between you and your companion has strengthened. When your companion is within 10 feet of you, and either you or your companion casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that would affect only one of you, you can instead have it affect both.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: You Have That Power Too
entries: The bond between you and your companion has strengthened. When your companion is within 10 feet of you, and either you or your companion casts a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that would affect only one of you, you can instead have it affect both.
At 11th level, your companion must be within 30 feet of you to benefit from this feature. At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Got Your Back
entries: Once per turn, when your companion is within 10 feet of you, and both you and your companion have to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the same effect, either you or your companion can choose to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the save. If either of you do so, the other of the two of you gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save. You can use this feature before or after you both make the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, but you must do so before the GM says whether the save succeeds or fails.
At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet of you to benefit from this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Got Your Back
entries: Once per turn, when your companion is within 10 feet of you, and both you and your companion have to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the same effect, either you or your companion can choose to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the save. If either of you do so, the other of the two of you gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the save. You can use this feature before or after you both make the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, but you must do so before the GM says whether the save succeeds or fails.
At 17th level, your companion must be within 60 feet of you to benefit from this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Now I Am The Master
entries: Your companion has learned almost all that it can from you. As an action on its turn, your companion can take the lead, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: It gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice its level.
Once per turn, when it deals damage or restores {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it can roll an additional die.
It gains {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic and energy damage.

entries: This effect ends early if your companion is {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or dies. Once your companion has used this feature, it can't use it again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Whills Order
entries: Monks of the Whills Order hold the secrets of the Force sacred, and dedicate their lives to defending ancient  knowledge of the Force and its artifacts. They master the use of ranged weapons, often crafting their own weapons in respectful admiration of the Jedi tradition of crafting {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}.

subclassFeature.name: Flurry of Light
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item Blaster pistol|sw5e-phb|blaster pistols}, {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb|blaster rifles}, ion pistols, ion rifles, and the lightbow, which are your Whills weapons and are monk weapons for you. When you are wielding a Whills weapon, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your Whills weapons count as melee weapons for you, and when you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with them, you deal kinetic damage equal to your Martial Arts Damage Die.

When you would make an unarmed strike using your Martial Arts {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} or as a part of your Flurry of Blows, you can instead attack with a Whills weapon you are wielding. You roll a {@dice d4} in place of the normal damage of your Whills weapon when attacking in this way. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the monk table.
When you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a Whills weapon, you can instead reload the weapon.

subclassFeature.name: The Force is With You
entries: As you channel the Force through you, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your Stunning Strike feature when you hit with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} while you are wielding a Whills weapon.

You can spend up to 3 focus points to reduce partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter). If you reduce the target below one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, you ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} bonuses entirely. At 17th level, you can spend 3 focus points to ignore {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|total cover}, as long as your target is not hidden from you.

When you hit a creature with a Whills weapon, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} against you until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: One With the Force
entries: You learn how to enter a trance, preparing to unleash yourself upon your enemy. While in this trance, you can still talk and move. If you stay in the trance for at least one minute, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, you can make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} on a number of creatures up to your focus ability modifier (a minimum of one) within 30 feet of you when you were in this trance.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Guided Strikes
entries: Your first ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and your first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} each turn deal additional damage equal to your focus ability modifier (a minimum of +1).

subclassFeature.name: Ysannanite Form
entries: {@optfeature Ysannanite Form|sw5e-phb}, also know as the Unorthodox Form, pairs the use of {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} with {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true}, seamlessly blending the two weapons to perform impressive feats. Those guardians who focus on the {@optfeature Ysannanite Form|sw5e-phb} are able to cut enemies down as efficiently with {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} as with blade.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple} and martial {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} that lack the two-handed property.

subclassFeature.name: Form Basics
entries: You gain the Ysannanite {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}, detailed in the {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb} Forms section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content. If you already know this form, you can instead choose another {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}.

subclassFeature.name: The Way of the Yerdua
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can take a meditative stance for 1 minute, granting you {@feat Supreme Accuracy|sw5e-phb|supreme accuracy} as you guide your shots to their target through the Force. While in this stance, you add your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1) to one ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and damage roll you make each turn. Additionally, when making a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You gain the following Channel the Force option.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Shots
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force and expend force points to deal additional damage to the target, which is the same type as the weapon's damage. The additional damage is 1d8 for each point spent in this way. You can't deal more additional damage than the amount shown in the Focused Strikes column of the guardian table.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Force-Empowered Shots
entries: Your familiarity with {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons has granted you greater insight into their function and usage. Once on each of your turns, drawing or stowing a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} no longer requires your object interaction. Additionally, you no longer require a free hand to reload.

At 11th level, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage. If you also use your Force-Empowered Shots with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Force-Empowered Shots. The damage is the same type as the weapon's damage.

subclassFeature.name: Phasestorm
entries: You can use your action to dart across the battlefield, striking up to six such creatures that you can see within 30 feet. You immediately move to each creature in succession without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}, after which you return to the space in which you started. Each creature must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with your weapon). A creature takes normal weapon damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. If you are wielding separate weapons in each hand with which you are proficient, a creature makes this save with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, and takes additional damage equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) on a failed save if the damage doesn't already include that modifier.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Master of the Unorthodox
entries: You've mastered the unity between {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} and blade. Your Dexterity and Wisdom or Charisma scores (your choice) increase by 2. Your maximum for these scores increases by 2. Additionally, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic, energy, and ion damage from weapons.

When you hit a creature with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} you make against that creature. When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} you make against that creature.

When you roll below half the maximum on a damage die, you can treat the roll as if you'd rolled half the maximum on the damage die. You can only affect a number of dice up to half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) in this way.

entries: This effect ends early if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Zoologist Pursuit
entries: Many academics develop an affinity for nature, studying the vast fauna that inhabit the different planets throughout the galaxy. Those scholars who choose the Zoologist Pursuit capitalize on their knowledge of animals, developing a strong bond with a companion with whom they gain an {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the battlefield.

subclassFeature.name: Wilderness Expert
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}) checks. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|sw5e-phb}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to forge a powerful bond with your own beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your number of available Hit Dice that can be spend to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is reduced by 1.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains a bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, damage rolls, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).
This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to forge a powerful bond with your own beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your number of available Hit Dice that can be spend to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is reduced by 1.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains a bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, damage rolls, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).
This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Beast Companion
entries: You learn to employ all the knowledge you've accumulated to forge a powerful bond with your own beast companion.
Create your beast companion as detailed in the Companions section of the Customization Options document for Expanded Content.
In addition to its traits and features, your beast companion gains additional benefits while it is bonded to you:

items: Your beast gains two additional traits. It gains one more additional trait when you reach 11th level in this class. For each beast trait in excess of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, your number of available Hit Dice that can be spend to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} is reduced by 1.

entries: Lastly, while bonded and within 10 feet of you, your beast companion gains a bonus to {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, damage rolls, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifer (minimum of +1).
This radius increases to 30 feet at 11th level, and 60 feet at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Vicious Hunting
entries: Your beast companion's strikes count as enhanced for the purpose of overcoming {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} and immunity to unenhanced attacks and damage. Additionally, when your beast makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you may expend a superiority die and apply the benefits of a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you know from this class, as if you had taken the action yourself.

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Agility
entries: Your beast's reflexes and agility allow it to move with a burst of {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. When your beast moves on its turn in combat, it can double its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of the turn. Once its used this feature, it can't use it again until it moves 0 feet on one of its turns.

subclassFeature.name: Feral Ferocity
entries: You have learned how to push your beast beyond its limits. If your beast is within 30 feet of you and can see or hear you, you can command it to enter a furious state. While raging, your beast gains the following benefits:

items: Your beast has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} if it is size Medium or larger.
Your beast has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity checks and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} if it is size Small or smaller.
When your beast hits with an attack, it deals bonus damage equal to your Critical Analysis ability modifer.
Your beast has {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic and energy damage.

entries: Your beast's furious state lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if your beast is knocked {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious}. You can end your beast's furious state as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Zoologist Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your studies in biology and behaviour of alien lifeforms. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Advantageous Companion
entries: When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}) check against a creature that can see your beast companion, and your companion is size Medium or larger, you make the check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check against a creature that can see your beast companion, and your companion is size Small or Tiny, you make the check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Holocam Attachment
entries: You have learned how to safely attach a holocam on the head of the companion. You learn the {@i tracker droid interface} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, your beast becomes a valid target of this power, and when you cast this power targeting your beast, you do so without spending tech points. You require use of a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} for this power.

entries.name: Neat Tricks
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} Your beast gains proficiency in one Strength or Dexterity skill of your choice. If your beast's size is Medium or larger and the chosen skill uses Strength, it has {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the chosen skill. If your beast's size is Small or smaller and the chosen skill uses Dexterity, it has {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the chosen skill.

entries.name: One Big Baddie
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Medium or larger beast} Your beast companion gains the following benefits:

items: It deals double damage against structures.
It can take the {@action Guard|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, but it can only guard you in this way.
It can spend a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to spend one of its Hit Dice to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

When it rolls a Hit Die to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the minimum number of {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} it can regain from the roll equals twice its Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

entries.name: Protective Friend
entries: If a creature makes a melee attack against you or your companion, and your companion is within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: The More the Merrier
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Size Small or smaller beast} Rather than a single beast companion, you instead control multiple beasts that function as a swarm. Your beast companion gains the following benefits:

items: Its effective size increases by two categories (from Tiny to Medium or Small to Large).
Its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to twice its level + 2.
It can only be mounted by creatures at least three size categories smaller than it, instead of one.
It can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a creature two size categories smaller than it.

While it is above half its hit point maximum, when it takes the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, it can make an additional attack. If the creature has the Extra Attack feature, this attack is in addition to the attack granted by that feature.
